name: PHQ-9 Depression Screening
description: Nine-question depression screener with an automatic total score and severity band (minimal to severe).
scoring: Each answer scores 0–3. The total (0–27) maps to minimal (0–4), mild (5–9), moderate (10–14), moderately severe (15–19) or severe (20–27) depression.
source: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2001, J Gen Intern Med 16:606 (PHQ-9). Codes: LOINC; form text as published at phqscreeners.com.

name: GAD-7 Anxiety Screening
description: Seven-question generalized anxiety screener with an automatic total score and severity band (minimal to severe).
scoring: Each answer scores 0–3. The total (0–21) maps to minimal (0–4), mild (5–9), moderate (10–14) or severe (15–21) anxiety.
source: Spitzer et al. 2006, Arch Intern Med 166:1092 (GAD-7). Codes: LOINC; form text as published at phqscreeners.com.
license: Developed by Drs. Robert L. Spitzer, Janet B.W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues, with an educational grant from Pfizer Inc. No permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.

name: AUDIT-C Alcohol Use Screening
description: Three-question alcohol consumption screen with an automatic total score (0–12) and the usual positive-screen thresholds.
scoring: Each answer scores 0–4. The total (0–12) is a positive screen at 4 or more for men and 3 or more for women.
source: Bush et al. 1998, Arch Intern Med 158:1789 (AUDIT-C, from the WHO AUDIT). Codes and answer lists: LOINC, as in the HL7 US Core AUDIT-C questionnaire.
license: No restrictions on use (per the ONC USCDI/ISP listing; submitted by NIAAA).

name: PHQ-2 Depression Screening
description: Two-question depression screener with an automatic total and positive-screen flag; the short entry to the PHQ-9.
scoring: Each answer scores 0–3. The total (0–6) is a positive screen at 3 or more.
source: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams 2003, Med Care 41:1284 (PHQ-2). Codes: LOINC; form text as published at phqscreeners.com.
license: Developed by Drs. Robert L. Spitzer, Janet B.W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues, with an educational grant from Pfizer Inc. No permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.

name: GAD-2 Anxiety Screening

source: Kroenke et al. 2007, Ann Intern Med 146:317 (GAD-2). Codes: LOINC; form text as published at phqscreeners.com.

name: qSOFA Sepsis Screen
description: Three bedside yes/no criteria with the qSOFA score and its risk result; two or more criteria mean a high risk of poor outcome.
scoring: Each criterion that is present scores 1 point. An unanswered criterion counts as No; the result appears once at least one criterion is answered.
source: Singer et al. 2016 (Sepsis-3), JAMA 315:801.
license: Original wording written for this builder; covered by the project license (non-commercial use with attribution; commercial use needs written permission). Formulas are published methods; see the source.

name: CHA₂DS₂-VASc Stroke Risk Score
description: Six yes/no criteria and the age with the CHA₂DS₂-VASc score (0–9) for stroke risk in atrial fibrillation; a higher score means a higher risk.
scoring: Points: heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age 75 or older 2, diabetes 1, previous stroke or TIA 2, vascular disease 1, age 65 to 74 1, female sex 1 (0–9). The score appears once the age is entered; an unanswered criterion counts as No.
source: Lip et al. 2010, Chest 137:263. Codes: LOINC.
license: Original wording written for this builder; covered by the project license (non-commercial use with attribution; commercial use needs written permission). Formulas are published methods; see the source.

name: Charlson Comorbidity Index
description: Comorbidities and age with the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index.
scoring: Comorbidities score 1, 2, 3 or 6 points by weight; the age adds 1 point per decade from 50, up to 4 points from age 80. The index appears once the age is entered; an unanswered comorbidity counts as No.
source: Charlson et al. 1987, J Chronic Dis 40:373; age adjustment per Charlson et al. 1994, J Clin Epidemiol 47:1245.

name: Glasgow Coma Scale
description: Eye, verbal and motor responses with the total score (3–15) and its severity band.
scoring: Eye 1–4, verbal 1–5 and motor 1–6 add up to a total of 3–15: 13–15 mild, 9–12 moderate, 3–8 severe.
source: Teasdale & Jennett 1974, Lancet 2:81 (Glasgow Coma Scale). Codes and answer lists: LOINC.

name: Apgar Score
description: The five Apgar criteria at 1 and 5 minutes after birth, each with its total (0–10) and result band.
scoring: Each criterion scores 0–2. The total (0–10) at each time point is reassuring at 7–10, moderately abnormal at 4–6 and low at 0–3.
source: Apgar 1953, Curr Res Anesth Analg 32:260 (Apgar score); score bands per AAP/ACOG. Codes and answer lists: LOINC.
